findings.reason: the node needs to settle from the owed entry's own recorded run and host (or name the ledger/caller that does), otherwise the route §8 wires misses exactly the cross-project copies it exists to reclaim.
findings.text: the plan says the launch path "settles the host's owed removals", but `garbage_collect_scratch` resolves attribution through one checkout's ledger (`_ledgered_run_ids(repo, project)` → `_gc_projects`, reckon/crew/gc.py:74-81, which enumerates only `<repo>/docs/state/*` when no project is given), so a launch for one project cannot settle a removal owed by a run that another mounted checkout ledgered — the run classifies as unattributed and falls to the age-based orphan sweep, which §8 says is for directories no run can be attributed to; the done-when's launch arm passes on a fixture whose owed run belongs to the launching project while the production case (a run resumed onto this host from a different project) is left unremoved for two hours

findings.reason: the section's goal is that a run's scratch leaves with it on every host, and as written the owed route leaves part of the scratch that the release route removes, so the two routes drift.
findings.text: the settlement route does not remove the same set as the release it stands in for: `remove_worker_scratch` also removes direct siblings named for the run's timestamp stem (reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:846-871, "A worker may create siblings named for the timestamp stem instead of placing every temporary file below TMPDIR"), while `garbage_collect_scratch` classifies only children named by run id (reckon/crew/gc.py:1123-1142), so a resumed attempt's sibling temp trees on the owing host survive the settlement even though the same host's local release would have taken them

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited symbol resolves: `ensure_worker_scratch`/`remove_worker_scratch` (reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:782, :829), `garbage_collect_scratch` (reckon/crew/gc.py:1173), the age-based `garbage_collect_orphan_scratch` (reckon/crew/gc.py:1030, SCRATCH_GRACE_SECONDS), `retention_sweep` (reckon/crew/gc.py:1329), and `_release_after_promotion` (reckon/crew/promotion_release.py:476), whose three named callers do call it (promotion.py:1125 and :1752, promotion_records.py:188, reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2590).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §8's done-when names measurable cases for the same-host release, the other-host release, its settlement by both a launch and a `retention_sweep` pass "whatever the copy's age", the two-host run, and the review promotion, and its negative control is the current code's own behaviour, which reports the wrong copy removed and so fails the second case.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the durable witness named is the committed evidence fragment, which §8 requires to quote each gate's command and summary line, and the gate logs it places under the run directory are transient by design as §3 says.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §8 names existing mechanism symbols and the leak measurement, with no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the two settlement routes §8 proposes do not reach the copies the release route removes.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one goal (a run's scratch leaves with the run on each host); repairing the review-promotion route is a further route to that same goal rather than a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — plan.html:22 records `s8: ["crew-state-stays-bounded#s7"]`, and §8 runs after the §7 sweep it extends (`retention_sweep`, reckon/crew/gc.py:1329), which has landed.
